commonLabels.description: Extra labels applied to every resource produced by the chart.

enabled.description: Emit ConfigMaps labelled for the Grafana sidecar to pick up (https://github.com/grafana/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/grafana). OPT-IN: requires your Grafana install to have dashboard sidecar enabled. Most operators ship dashboards via their own GitOps, this stays out of the way by default.

label.description: Label the Grafana sidecar searches for. Most installs use `grafana_dashboard=1`; adjust if yours differs.

fullnameOverride.description: Optional override of the chart's full name (used as resource name prefix).

annotations.description: Extra annotations on the Gateway resource (e.g. for external-dns / cert-manager integration).

enabled.description: **Recommended.** Create a Gateway API Gateway + GRPCRoute. Gateway API is the Kubernetes-recommended successor to Ingress (<https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/>). Requires a Gateway API implementation in the cluster — Envoy Gateway (<https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/>) is a common pick and what we test against.

envoyBackendTrafficPolicy.description: Envoy Gateway BackendTrafficPolicy targeting the validator GRPCRoute. Bumps the upstream cluster's circuit-breaker limits and HTTP/2 stream cap so bursty browser-driven gRPC-Web traffic doesn't hit Envoy's defaults (max_connections=1024, max_pending_requests= 1024, max_requests=1024) and surface to clients as 503 with `response_flags=UO` (upstream overflow). Browsers mislabel these 503s as CORS errors because no Allow-Origin header rides on a 5xx response — without this policy a public validator looks broken from a browser when traffic spikes even though the proxy itself is healthy.  Envoy Gateway only — opt-in for portability. Other Gateway API implementations need their own equivalent (e.g. Istio `DestinationRule.connectionPool`).

timeout.description: Passed through 1:1 to BackendTrafficPolicy spec.timeout (tcp/http duration knobs). Structure validated by the Envoy Gateway CRD at apply time.

envoyClientTrafficPolicy.description: Envoy Gateway ClientTrafficPolicy targeting the validator Gateway (downstream client side). Opt-in. timeout passed through 1:1 to spec.timeout; validated by the Envoy Gateway CRD at apply time.

hostname.description: Hostname for the validator. external-dns can manage the corresponding DNS record from this annotation.

tlsSecretName.description: TLS Secret produced by cert-manager (or any other source).

repository.description: Image repository for the linera binaries (REQUIRED).

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to .Chart.appVersion if empty.

enabled.description: **DEPRECATED / maintenance mode.** Create a Kubernetes Ingress. The Kubernetes project has placed the Ingress API in feature freeze and recommends Gateway API for new deployments — see <https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/>. Prefer the `gateway` block below for new installs. This option is kept for operators whose clusters only ship an Ingress controller.

backtrace.description: RUST_BACKTRACE value. "0" (default): no Rust stack traces in logs. Anyhow error chains (`0: ..., 1: ...`) are still emitted — those are the useful part; only the tokio runtime frames disappear. "1":           short backtrace (file + line per frame). "full":        full symbolic backtrace. Only set this when actively debugging — it makes routine errors look like panics.

level.description: RUST_LOG value applied to every linera process.

nameOverride.description: Optional override of the chart name.

networkName.description: Network identifier (used for service discovery in some optional subcomponents). Free-form, e.g. "testnet-conway" or "my-network".

defaultDeny.description: Add a deny-all NetworkPolicy that covers every pod in the release namespace. Only flip on if you've audited the other workloads in this namespace — this will break any pod that lacks an explicit allow rule.

enabled.description: Emit NetworkPolicy resources (proxy + shards + optional default-deny). Harmless on clusters without an enforcer.

extraEgress.description: Extra egress rules, appended to both proxy and shard policies. Must include at least your storage backend (ScyllaDB, RocksDB sidecar endpoint, etc.) and any observability push targets.

metricsScrapeFrom.description: Sources allowed to scrape /metrics on proxies + shards. Common override: your Prometheus / Alloy namespace.

proxyIngressFrom.description: Sources allowed to reach the proxy on the client port. Leave empty to allow from anywhere (public gRPC endpoint). Typical override: restrict to an ingress/gateway namespace.

otlpExporterEndpoint.description: OpenTelemetry OTLP endpoint. Empty = tracing disabled.

metrics.description: Prometheus metrics port (every component listens here).

proxy.description: gRPC port the proxy listens on for client connections.

shard.description: gRPC port for shard inter-process communication.

enabled.description: Create a PrometheusRule with the default Linera alerts (validator down, shard restart, proxy high latency). Extend with extraRules below. OPT-IN: requires prometheus-operator + the PrometheusRule CRD installed in the cluster.

extraRules.description: Additional alert / recording rules merged into the default set.

labels.description: Extra labels on the PrometheusRule (match your Prometheus's ruleSelector if it filters by label).

recordingRules.description: Pre-computed recording rules (`linera:*:rate1m` aggregates over execution, request, storage, view metrics). Useful when a local monitoring stack answers Grafana queries and you want faster long-window panels. Leave OFF when metrics are forwarded to a central backend that already does its own recording.

cli.description: linera-proxy CLI flags. Same conventions as shards.cli (every flag is the values currently in use on the testnet-conway validators.

nodeSelector.description: Pod scheduling. Default podAntiAffinity (hard, by hostname) keeps each proxy on a distinct node so PDB minAvailable holds during a node drain. Operators on a single-node cluster must override `affinity` here OR keep replicas: 1.

podDisruptionBudget.description: PodDisruptionBudget for the proxy pods. Protects against simultaneous evictions during node drains / voluntary disruptions. Set only one of `minAvailable` / `maxUnavailable`. Not created for shards by design: each shard holds a unique slice of validator state, so any voluntary disruption is a correctness risk — operators must drain shards manually.

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum proxy pods that may be unavailable at once. Leave unset when `minAvailable` is used.

minAvailable.description: Minimum proxy pods that must stay available (integer or percentage string like "50%"). Mutually exclusive with `maxUnavailable`.

replicas.description: Number of proxy replicas. Default 2 + PDB minAvailable=1 below tolerates one node drain without losing client-facing traffic. Single-node clusters must set replicas: 1 and disable podDisruptionBudget.

resources.description: Resource requests and limits. Defaults sized from observed steady state on the testnet-conway production validators (GKE, no resource cap historically): linera-proxy plateaus around 3.5 GiB p50 / 4.0 GiB p95 / 5.0 GiB max per replica, with ~0.45 cpu p95 and ~0.66 cpu max. Set as Burstable QoS. Operators with very different traffic should override here.

annotations.description: Annotations on the proxy Service (e.g. cloud LB hints).

loadBalancerIP.description: Optional static IP (for cloud providers that respect this).

type.description: Service type. ClusterIP for in-cluster only, LoadBalancer for cloud LBs, NodePort for bare-metal exposure.

annotations.description: Annotations applied to the ServiceAccount (useful for workload-identity setups).

name.description: ServiceAccount name. Empty = derived from chart name.

enabled.description: Create a ServiceMonitor so a Prometheus Operator can scrape both shards and proxies. OPT-IN: most operators wire scraping with their own observability stack, this chart stays out of the way. Enable only if you run prometheus-operator in the same cluster.

labels.description: Extra labels on the ServiceMonitor (e.g. release: prometheus if your Prometheus selects by that label).

cli.description: linera-server CLI flags. Every flag is passed as `--<kebab-case-key> <value>` and is omitted entirely when the value is null. Defaults are the values currently in use on the Linera testnet-conway validators. Override per cluster as needed.

extraArgs.description: Free-form extra arguments appended verbatim to the linera-server command line. Each entry is added on its own line.

extraEnv.description: Extra environment variables added to the shard container.

extraVolumes.description: Extra volumes / volume mounts (for advanced use cases).

livenessProbe.description: Probe overrides. Empty = sensible defaults baked into the template.

nodeSelector.description: Pod scheduling. Default podAntiAffinity (hard, by hostname) keeps each shard on a distinct node so a single node loss takes out at most one shard. Operators on smaller clusters (fewer nodes than shard replicas) must override `affinity` here OR add more nodes, otherwise excess shards stay Pending.

podLabels.description: Pod labels (in addition to the default app.kubernetes.io/* labels).

resources.description: Resource requests and limits. Defaults sized from observed steady state on the testnet-conway production validators (GKE, no resource cap historically): linera-server plateaus around 6.8 GiB p50 / 8.5 GiB p95 / 9.5 GiB max per shard, with bursty <0.5 cpu p95 and ~0.6 cpu max. Set as Burstable QoS — req covers steady state, lim covers plateau + ~25 % headroom. Operators with very different chain workloads should override here.

serverTokioThreads.description: Tokio worker threads per shard. Empty = one per CPU (Tokio default).

dual.description: Enable dual storage mode (RocksDB local + ScyllaDB remote). Recommended for development only.

replicationFactor.description: Storage replication factor (must match the ScyllaDB cluster RF).

rocksdbSize.description: RocksDB volume size per shard (only used when storage.dual is true).

rocksdbStorageClass.description: StorageClass for the RocksDB PVCs. Empty = cluster default.

uri.description: Connection string passed to --storage. Default points to a ScyllaDB cluster in the "scylla" namespace (what the linera-validator-stack umbrella chart provisions). Override for a different backend.

useComponentPrefix.description: Prefix component resource names (StatefulSets/Services) with `<fullname>-`. Default false = clean names (proxy, shards, proxy-internal) matching what linera-network-init mints. Set true for legacy deployments whose minted server config references the prefixed names.

existingSecret.description: Use an existing Secret instead of inlining configs above. The Secret must contain two keys: "serverConfig" and "genesisConfig".

genesisConfigData.description: Genesis config JSON (public). Distributed to every validator in the same network. Inline as a string here, or use existingSecret.

serverConfigData.description: Server config JSON (PRIVATE — contains the validator signing key). Inline as a string here, or use existingSecret.

validatorLabel.description: Validator label exposed to external monitoring systems. Free-form, e.g. "validator-1" or "us-east-pilot".
